title: Map CANMAT assessment guidance to the starter MDD workup
proposedRouting: Review CANMAT Q.1.d and Table 1.2 against the patient-owned facts and each current workup objective; decide which questions are essential, optional, or low-value for this specific starter presentation.
guidance: Resolved qualitative direction: assessment relevance follows the focused patient and the submitted intervention, not a universal checklist. Episode course and depressive symptoms are central to this initial-MDD snapshot; antidepressant selection activates mania history; any medication start activates medication reconciliation and allergy/adverse-reaction history; substance history is broadly rewarded; and the resolved passive wish for death keeps detailed safety assessment central. CANMAT informs the assessment direction, while the trigger architecture and game weighting remain separately attributable Developer opinion.
reviewerNotes: Approved by Dustin Rowland. P1: depressive-symptom history is encounter-specific, not universally required. P2: episode course and depressive syndrome are central to this initial-MDD decision. P3: mania screening is treatment-triggered and should matter strongly for antidepressants, with later medication-specific refinement possible. P4: medication reconciliation is activated by starting a medication and may later be fulfilled by staff automation. P5: allergy/adverse-reaction history is activated by starting a medication. P6: a resolved prior reaction affects safety whether or not the player revealed it. P7: substance-use history should be rewarded broadly in depression, anxiety, and other commonly substance-induced presentations. Use provisional point values and keep concern, certainty, trigger, and consequence independently auditable.
resurfacingTrigger: When the starter MDD patient facts, action costs, CBC/TSH profiles, or assessment evidence changes.

resolution.note: Added approved qualitative diagnosis-owned assessment and prerequisite rules, generic treatment-triggered workup requirements, concern/certainty trace metadata, and a separate pre-resolved prior-reaction safety layer. The prototype uses provisional points; no routine laboratory panel was made mandatory, and the generic reaction-severity mapping remains medically unreviewed.

title: Decide the starter MDD severity and initial-treatment modality
proposedRouting: First assign a clinically supported severity and safety-risk profile from structured patient facts, then compare the database route and alternative routes with CANMAT Q.3.a and Q.3.b.
guidance: The current case rewards an antidepressant plus psychotherapy and penalizes omission of psychotherapy. CANMAT distinguishes mild, moderate, and severe episodes: psychotherapy may be preferred for mild illness, psychotherapy or antidepressant medication may each be an initial option for moderate illness, and combined treatment is emphasized more strongly for severe illness. Decide what severity this patient actually represents and whether medication-only, psychotherapy-only, and combined routes should each be accepted or differently weighted.
reviewerNotes: Psychiatrist/developer direction: align psychotherapy and medication as peer treatment modalities. When the reviewed algorithm ranks them equally, either one appropriate medication or one appropriate psychotherapy is a complete acceptable treatment. Add a combination bonus only when the algorithm ranks combination treatment more highly. A compatible medication-plus-therapy combination that the algorithm does not address remains acceptable and neutral. Evaluate the whole set for parsimony: selecting several primary psychotherapy types or multiple same-role antidepressants is shotgun treatment unless an explicit pathway supports it; dangerous or duplicate medication combinations receive their safety consequence. Investigation shotgun behavior should also lose points, ordinarily through cumulative action costs rather than duplicate clinical penalties.
resurfacingTrigger: When severity facts, safety facts, psychotherapy availability, or initial-treatment guidance changes.

title: Set the broad first-line antidepressant baseline and fit modifiers
proposedRouting: Review CANMAT Q.3.e and Tables 3.3 through 3.5 for the broad current pathway. Use only the verified abstract of Bostwick 2010 to nominate candidate fit dimensions; require current, legally processable evidence and separate psychiatrist review before assigning medication-specific directions or point values.
guidance: Resolved qualitative direction: in a focused uncomplicated adult MDD snapshot already routed to medication, one reviewed member of the current five-medication first-line set receives equal dominant primary-route credit. CANMAT and the accepted Developer opinion remain separate provenance records. Medication-specific sleep, weight, sexual-function, prior-response, preference, feasibility, interaction, and safety effects remain smaller independent layers. The provisional 200-point route value and existing fit values are game-balance guesses for later patient review, not source-supplied magnitudes.
reviewerNotes: Approved by Dustin Rowland: use one broad first-line antidepressant pathway with equal primary baseline, preserve medication-specific fit as nontrivial smaller modifiers, and make the best provisional point estimate now for later case-by-case tuning.
resurfacingTrigger: When the starter formulary, medication files, patient fit facts, or antidepressant guidance changes.

resolution.note: Added one reviewed diagnosis-owned qualitative rule and a shared mdd-initial-first-line medication tag for the five currently modeled medications. The prototype and initial Reviewer policy now use one 200-point broad grade; medication fit remains separately itemized, and the exact score magnitudes remain medically unreviewed provisional balance.

title: Review psychotherapy options and weights for the starter MDD case
proposedRouting: Compare CANMAT Q.3.c and Table 3.2 with the treatment catalog and current predicates, keeping therapy types as separate catalog entries rather than prose aliases.
guidance: CANMAT identifies CBT, IPT, and behavioral activation as first-line psychological treatments for acute MDD. The current rule treats supportive psychotherapy as equivalent to CBT and IPT, while behavioral activation receives a separate additive reward. Decide which therapies satisfy the broad pathway, which deserve fit modifiers, and whether additive scoring currently double-counts one treatment modality.
resurfacingTrigger: When psychotherapy catalog entries, availability rules, patient preference facts, or psychological-treatment evidence changes.

title: Calibrate outpatient and escalation scoring from structured safety facts
proposedRouting: Review CANMAT Q.2.c and Q.3.a alongside the exact structured suicide, psychosis, impairment, and medical facts; then adjudicate both under-escalation and disproportionate escalation values.
guidance: The current patient has an authored passive wish for death but no current active ideation, preparatory behavior, or attempt history, and the case strongly penalizes urgent or emergency escalation. Decide whether those facts support routine outpatient care and whether -180 and -500 are proportionate game penalties. The engine should not infer outpatient suitability from a narrative sentence; it should derive scoring only from structured facts and the reviewed rule.
resurfacingTrigger: When structured safety facts, severity, disposition capabilities, or safety-risk guidance changes.

title: Source the bupropion and controlled-seizure-history judgment
proposedRouting: Review current regulatory labeling, seizure-risk data, and clinically relevant evidence separately. Preserve the psychiatrist/developer interpretation as its own future opinion record even if publications are attached; do not turn a contextual study into a blanket guideline recommendation.
guidance: Psychiatrist/developer opinion to source: bupropion may sometimes be used in a patient whose seizure disorder is well controlled, but it is almost never a good or first option in that setting. The future rule should distinguish a heavily penalized relative risk from an absolute hard block when the reviewed facts support that nuance. No point value or active fit rule is authorized by this ticket.
resurfacingTrigger: When bupropion safety evidence, regulatory labeling, seizure-history facts, or contraindication-severity policy changes.

title: Choose a bounded MDD severity generator policy
proposedRouting: Keep mild, moderate, and severe MDD inside the single MDD diagnosis-family record. Patient templates select an intended branch and add narrow constraints; the generator validates separate symptom, function, psychosis, and safety dimensions against a reviewed envelope and retries or quarantines conflicts.
guidance: The ownership question is resolved: MDD owns its reusable mild, moderate, and severe variants; a patient template may request moderate MDD but must not redefine generic moderate-MDD parameters. The remaining clinical question is the bounded content of each severity envelope. Current sources use non-equivalent schemes: treatment guidelines use qualitative mild/moderate/severe or less/more severe groupings, while PHQ-9 bands measure symptom burden and do not by themselves establish diagnosis or episode severity. Psychosis and acute safety remain separately explainable and cannot disappear inside one total score. All three severity branches stay disabled until the envelope and provenance receive psychiatrist review. This ticket authorizes no clinical threshold, treatment, or point change.
reviewerNotes: Architecture direction accepted: variants of an underlying disorder belong to one diagnosis-family record. A patient template can select moderate MDD and add patient-specific specifiers or constraints, but the MDD record owns the reusable mild/moderate/severe parameters.
resurfacingTrigger: Before enabling any MDD severity branch or generating severity-dependent MDD treatment pathways.

title: Review sleep as an antidepressant-fit dimension
proposedRouting: Review therapeutic sleep fit separately from treatment-emergent somnolence or insomnia. A medication's sedating adverse effect must not automatically become evidence that it treats baseline insomnia.
guidance: CANMAT identifies sleep disturbance as a potential selection factor and lists mirtazapine as an option with evidence for sleep disturbance. Current meta-analyses can separately inform therapeutic sleep outcomes and treatment-emergent sleep harms, but they do not select a point value or prove that every sedating medication is a good insomnia treatment. Decide the qualitative direction first; keep the active +35 modifier provisional.
resurfacingTrigger: Before approving or changing any sleep-linked antidepressant fit modifier.

title: Decide when TSH is high-yield in a depression workup
proposedRouting: Choose whether uncomplicated depressive symptoms make TSH optional and defensible or routinely high-yield, then separately decide whether the starter patient's fatigue plus weight gain crosses that boundary.
guidance: CANMAT makes TSH a defensible low-cost contributor check while also stating that direct evidence for routine bloodwork is limited. Current screening evidence supports stronger relevance for an explicit thyroid history, thyroid-affecting medication, abnormal thyroid examination, or coherent multi-feature thyroid syndrome, and does not justify making a normal result retroactively low-value. Fatigue and modest weight change are nonspecific. Review the clinical category only; exact trigger counts and game points remain separate Developer and balance decisions.
resurfacingTrigger: Before approving a reusable TSH objective or changing its reward or omission penalty in the starter MDD patient.

title: Review weight and metabolic antidepressant fit
proposedRouting: Review average short-term medication-associated weight direction separately from a BMI-specific penalty, diabetes-specific risk, long-term outcomes, contraindications, and game-point magnitude.
guidance: Current evidence supports meaningful average short-term physiological differences among antidepressants and supports considering patient presentation and preference. It does not directly establish that high BMI changes the individual effect, that mirtazapine causes a specific long-term diabetes outcome, or that either drug becomes contraindicated. Decide whether a small weight-preference direction is acceptable while keeping the active -50 high-BMI modifier and diabetes rule unresolved.
resurfacingTrigger: Before approving or changing any weight-, BMI-, or diabetes-linked antidepressant fit modifier.

title: Review sexual effects and adherence as fit dimensions
proposedRouting: Review baseline sexual function, medication-associated sexual effects, general adverse-effect burden, and medication-specific adherence predictions as separate propositions.
guidance: CANMAT supports asking about baseline sexual function and considering adverse-effect differences, including lower-sexual-adverse-effect options. Current pooled evidence supports an SSRI-class sexual-effect dimension and only a general relationship between adverse-effect burden and adherence. It does not provide a complete medication ranking or justify medication-specific adherence points. Keep baseline sexual function and medication-emergent sexual effects inside structured medication tolerability, tied to a specific regimen or prior-trial entry. A published source rate must retain population, outcome definition, time horizon, and uncertainty; it must not silently become the game's generation probability.
reviewerNotes: Developer opinion: sexual history and medication-associated sexual effects belong in medication tolerability, tied to the relevant current medication or prior trial. They may be generated as present only from a medication-specific, source-backed rate profile; unknown must remain distinct from absent. Review the source-to-game probability mapping before activation.
resurfacingTrigger: When a medication-specific sexual-adverse-effect source or rate profile is added, or before activating a sexual-function fit modifier.

title: Separate combination, adjunctive treatment, and shotgun starts
proposedRouting: Decide whether the future regimen model must store treatment intent explicitly rather than inferring combination, adjunctive treatment, or shotgun prescribing from medication count alone.
guidance: CANMAT defines combination as starting two treatments together and adjunctive treatment as adding to an existing treatment. Recent pooled evidence also prevents treating every antidepressant pair as intrinsically dangerous. The current prototype may retain a strong case-specific parsimony consequence for starting several same-role treatments, but a reusable safety finding should require an actual duplicate mechanism, interaction, contraindication, or case-supported hazard. Review this taxonomy separately from any point value.
resurfacingTrigger: Before a normalized regimen evaluator or another multi-medication patient uses medication count as a clinical predicate.

title: Separate switch and adjunctive routes after inadequate response
proposedRouting: Review no response, partial response, tolerability, and adverse effects as separate structured inputs before choosing a switch or adjunctive route. Keep benefit, additive burden, interactions, cost, and adherence as separate trace contributors.
guidance: CANMAT generally favors switching after no response or troublesome adverse effects and considers adjunctive treatment after partial response with good tolerability. This is an adult community-MDD boundary, not a universal psychiatric regimen rule. Decide whether this qualitative branch is appropriate for the focused inadequate-response patients before any score or treatment grade changes.
resurfacingTrigger: Before revising the adequate-nonresponse, prior-intolerance, or augmentation review patients.

title: Require an explicit medication transition state
proposedRouting: Decide whether overlap may receive a transition exemption only when the source regimen entry, destination medication, switching strategy, and pair compatibility are explicit. A start-plus-stop checklist alone must not imply a safe cross-taper.
guidance: CANMAT distinguishes crossover and washout strategies from simultaneous combination treatment and identifies pair-specific exceptions such as MAOI washout requirements. The current snapshot model has no dosing or time simulation, so the smallest future representation is a categorical transition intent plus pair-specific compatibility—not an inferred timeline. Review the boundary only; do not implement cross-titration or assign points from this ticket.
resurfacingTrigger: Before adding cross-titration, medication-overlap exemptions, or a patient whose immediate best step is a medication switch.
